## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `SetupGuide`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `sap-s4hana-api-sales-quotation-srv-setup`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **SetupGuide**.

## Step 2: Activate the sales quotation OData service

1. <!-- manual: Log on to the SAP S/4HANA system with a basis administrator user. -->
2. <!-- manual: Open transaction SOAMANAGER (Service-Oriented Architecture Manager). -->
3. <!-- manual: Under Web Service Configuration, search for the service API_SALES_QUOTATION_SRV. -->
4. Select the service entry and select **Activate** to expose it for external HTTP calls.
5. Alternatively, open transaction **SICF** (HTTP Service Hierarchy), navigate to `/sap/opu/odata/sap/API_SALES_QUOTATION_SRV`, right-select the node, and select **Activate Service**.

## Step 3: Assign authorization roles to the API user

1. <!-- manual: Open transaction SU01 (User Maintenance) and select the SAP user account that will call the API. -->
2. <!-- manual: Go to the Roles tab and assign one of the following: -->
3. The standard SAP role `SAP_SD_BC_SALES_QUOTATION_ALL`, which grants full access to the Sales Quotation API.
4. A custom authorization role containing authorization object `S_SERVICE` with `SRV_NAME = API_SALES_QUOTATION_SRV` and `SRV_TYPE = HT`.
5. <!-- manual: Additionally, ensure the user has SD document authorizations, for example: -->
6. <!-- manual: Authorization object V_VBAK_AAT with activity 01 (Create), 02 (Change), 03 (Display) for document type QT. -->
7. <!-- manual: Authorization object V_VBAK_VKO covering the relevant sales organizations. -->
8. <!-- manual: Save the user record and, if required, regenerate the authorization profile via transaction SU25 or PFCG. -->

## Step 4: Retrieve the hostname and port

1. The **hostname** is the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) or IP address of your SAP S/4HANA application server (e.g., `s4hana.example.com`).
2. The default HTTPS port is **443**. Confirm the actual port with your SAP basis team if a non-standard port is configured.
3. <!-- manual: Validate connectivity by opening the service metadata document in a browser: A successful response returns an XML document describing the OData entity model. -->

## Step 5: Obtain API user credentials

1. <!-- manual: Use an existing SAP dialog user or create a dedicated Communication User of type System or Communication via transaction SU01. -->
2. <!-- manual: Set a password for the user and ensure the account is not locked. -->
3. Note the **username** and **password**; these are supplied as `auth.username` and `auth.password` in the connector `ConnectionConfig`.
